calls.reasoning: Q3 2026 guidance is operating income of $22.5-26.5B. Amazon has beaten the top of its range 8 quarters running (Q2: $27.5B against a $20-24B guide), so I expect about $27.5-28.5B. After small net interest and other items, a ~20% tax rate and ~10.95B diluted shares, that gives core GAAP EPS of about $2.05-2.15. Street consensus is $1.96-2.03, and Amazon beats it most quarters. The main risk to the range is Anthropic. Q1 ($2.78) and Q2 ($5.75) were inflated by markups on the nonvoting preferred stock, which is only remeasured when there is an observable transaction. No priced Anthropic round in Jul-Sep was found, and the IPO is targeted for November (Q4). Gains on the convertible notes sit in AOCI and only hit earnings on conversion, and past conversions happened in Q1. So I put ~9% on Anthropic-type gains pushing EPS above $2.995 and ~1.5% on a large charge or markdown pushing it below $0.995.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the key facts: Q2 EPS of $5.75 driven by a $53.4B Anthropic gain, the Q3 guide of $22.5-26.5B, consensus of $1.96-2.03, no Q3 Anthropic primary round found, and an IPO targeted for Q4. Their medians are tightly clustered ($2.09-2.12), and I agree with that core build. The remaining disagreements are judgment calls. (1) Tax rate, 18% vs 21%: this moves EPS by about $0.08, so I used ~20% and kept the width at 0.57. (2) Size of the upside escape, 8% vs 12%: no dossier found a qualifying Q3 transaction, but secondary trades in 'similar securities' could in principle trigger a remeasurement and the searches cannot be exhaustive, so I chose 9%. (3) Whether a Polymarket market exists: Runs 1 and 2 report a thin market (~$2.9k volume) on EPS above $2.00 at about 64% Yes; Run 3 found none. I could not check this without web access. Either way it is a different contract and too thin to anchor on, though it is consistent with my distribution. I also added a small downside escape that Runs 1 and 3 omitted, for a large charge, impairment or equity markdown (Q3 2025 included a $2.5B FTC charge).
